To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the phytoavailability of added Cs to allophanic soil decreased rapidly within about 100 d, and that the rate of the decrease was related to the contribution of Cs specific sites to the total cation exchange sites in the soil.
the phytoavailability of added Cs decreased with incubation time in the soil and that this decreasing rate was affected by soil types.
phytoavailability and extractability of Cs in soil decreased with incubation time, and the decreasing rates varied among soil types.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the temporal changes in the phytoavailability and extractability of added Cs in soil.
the temporal change of phytoavailability and extractability of radiocaesium in allophanic Ando soils.

the time-dependent changes of phyloavailability of Cs in soil, and the results suggest that the decreasing rates of phytoavailability in early period after the Cs deposition are dependent on the types of soil.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the aging effect of the radiocaesium in soil was not negligible during early period after its deposition.

the phytoavailable Cs in allophanic Ando-sol is gradually lost with time, and that this process can be quantitatively evaluated by using the soil-to-plant trans-fer factors or the extractabilities of Cs.
radiocaesium added to the soil is gradually fixed to soil minerals, but the fixation rates are dependent on soil type and time elapsed after the deposition.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the aging effect of Cs on the phytoavailability is not so strong for the allophanic soils, and the extractability test by 1 M ammonium acetate may be a useful method to estimate the aging effect of the Cs in the soils.
the phytoavailability of added Cs in Andosols decreased rapidly during early period after its deposition and then gradually decreased thereafter, which may also be true for radiocaesium.
the phytoavailability of added Cs decreased with the incubation time in all the soil samples and that the decreasing rate was faster in the Andosols than in the non-andosols.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the phytoavailability of added stable Cs was gradually lost with the passage of time, which is consistent with previous studies on radiocaesium in the field.
the extractability of Cs by water or 1 M NH _{4} OAc solution can be used as a surrogate for the phytoavailability of soil Cs in early period after the Cs deposition.

the transfer factors of stable Cs from the allophanic soils to grasses decreased rapidly during the early period after its addition to the soils, and the decreasing rates were similar to each other among the allophanic soil samples.
